fixes.explanation: Close, because the lamp does show up a couple of verses later (1 Samuel 3:3). But the text says this happens "Before the lamp of God had gone out…" so it was still burning. The thing that was scarce was the word of the LORD, along with visions. That's the difference in those days.
Right. He runs to Eli and says, "Here I am, for you have called me." That tells us Samuel thinks Eli is the one who called. The text also says Samuel "…did not yet know the LORD…" (1 Samuel 3:7).
It's actually true. Samuel ran to Eli and said, "Here I am, for you have called me." That's Samuel saying Eli called him. The text also says Samuel "…did not yet know the LORD…" (1 Samuel 3:7).
Not quite. The text says Samuel "…got up, went to Eli…" and said again, "Here I am, for you have called me." Staying in bed to listen isn't what the text shows. That boy was up and moving.

You've got it. The text says Samuel "…did not yet know the LORD, because the word of the LORD had not yet been revealed to him." Twice he heard his name and ran to Eli, and this is what the text tells us about him right then. The word of the LORD hadn't been revealed to him yet.

He's already there. The text says Samuel was lying down in the temple of the LORD, where the ark of God was located (1 Samuel 3:3). What hasn't happened yet is the word of the LORD being revealed to him (1 Samuel 3:7). That's the one the text names.
Yes, on the third call. The text says, "Then Eli realized that it was the LORD who was calling the boy." It took three rounds, but Eli put it together.
It's true, friend. The text says, "Then Eli realized that it was the LORD who was calling the boy." It took three calls before he got there. But he got there.
Yes. The text says, "Then the LORD came and stood there, calling as before, 'Samuel! Samuel!'" This time the LORD Himself comes and stands there. That's the difference on this call.
Not through Eli. The text says the LORD Himself "…came and stood there…" Eli told Samuel what to say (1 Samuel 3:9), but the calling came from the LORD.
Yes, Eli. The LORD says, "On that day I will carry out against Eli everything I have spoken about his house, from beginning to end." This is a heavy word. It's about Eli's house.
The text doesn't mention anyone forbidding him. It says Samuel "…was afraid to tell Eli the vision…" The feeling the text gives is fear. That's the word that fits.
Right. The text says, "…Samuel told him everything and did not hide a thing from him." That's everything, with nothing hidden. Even after being afraid to tell it (1 Samuel 3:15), he told it all.
That's Eli's answer. He says, "He is the LORD… Let Him do what is good in His eyes." It's a reply after hard news, and I think it sounds calm. I think that took something.
